description: Adds the business's own pictures: product shots, the products in use (lifestyle), brand pictures, and posts it already published (use post: their look, finish, light and palette is what Marsell's new pictures share, never their subject or words). Each one from a public https url or its bytes (data_base64), with a caption saying what it shows, its use, and the product's name when it shows one. A picture of one of the business's own characters (named first with add_characters) gives character and the look it shows, and it becomes that character in that look, kept exactly as pictured; a picture of its own place (named with add_places) gives place. Send clean pictures of each look (a character sheet or a render on a plain ground), not frames where it is small or among other things. Say when a screen of its product shows a demo, a sample or a client's brand rather than the business's own. PNG, JPEG or WebP (an SVG is drawn to a PNG). They become the project's pictures, which Marsell reads after the owner confirms and uses as references for the pictures it makes. As many as the business has. For files on the agent's own machine, get_upload_link gives an address to send them to from your shell, so nothing big passes through your messages.

pictures.description: One or more pictures, each from a url or its bytes, with its caption.

character.description: The business's own character it shows (a mascot, a host), by its name in add_characters; the picture joins that character.

data_base64.description: Or the file's bytes, base64 (as large as one MCP message carries, about 4 MB).

filename.description: Its file name with its extension, when you have one.

look.description: With character: which of its looks this is ("3D", "drawn flat"), by its name in add_characters.

place.description: The business's own place it shows, by its name in add_places; the picture joins that place.

product.description: The product it shows, by its name in add_products.

url.description: A public https address of the file. Marsell fetches it itself (public addresses only, up to 8 MB).

use.description: post: a post the business already published, kept for its look.

name: add_pictures
title: Add pictures
